query: High-entropy alloys contain five or more elements at 5–35 at% each, generally with comparable atomic radii. Refractory and nickel-based high-entropy alloys have demonstrated elevated-temperature mechanical properties comparable to titanium- and nickel-based alloys used in extreme environments because of their heat resistance and specific strength. However, prior investigations have mainly treated titanium and nickel as additions, leaving alloys in which both are primary constituents unexplored. Subject to the stated compositional definition, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted relative outcome, composition and operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The application of high-pressure torsion (HPT) with optimized conditions can refine the grain structure and develop a favorable texture, leading to enhanced mechanical properties at elevated temperatures in a TiNiCrFeCo high-entropy alloy.
generation.conditions: Elevated temperature (900°C) and high stress (600 MPa)
generation.mechanism: Severe plastic deformation and grain boundary engineering
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and ductility by 20% and 30%, respectively
generation.uncertainty: The optimized HPT conditions and the resulting microstructure and properties of the TiNiCrFeCo alloy are uncertain and require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of TiNiCrFeCo alloys with and without HPT under the same operating conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HPT-treated alloy does not show significant improvements in yield strength and ductility compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
